scenarioStory.history: Coworker witnessed patient collapse at her desk into generalized tonic-clonic convulsions and called 911 immediately. Seizure activity has been continuous for approximately 6 minutes by the time EMS arrives. Coworker reports patient has a known seizure disorder but mentioned running out of her medication earlier in the week.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old female actively seizing on the floor, generalized tonic-clonic movements ongoing, per bystander for approximately 6 minutes already. → Positioned and IM midazolam given: Crew protects the airway, applies oxygen, checks blood glucose while still seizing, and administers weight-based IM midazolam without delaying for IV access. → Seizure resolves after midazolam: Convulsive activity has stopped; patient is postictal with confusion, depressed but spontaneous respirations, and gradually returning responsiveness.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old female actively seizing on the floor, generalized tonic-clonic movements ongoing, per bystander for approximately 6 minutes already.

scenarioEvents.name: Positioned and IM midazolam given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew protects the airway, applies oxygen, checks blood glucose while still seizing, and administers weight-based IM midazolam without delaying for IV access.
relatedChecklist: Position patient laterally; suction oral secretions to maintain airway patency
Apply oxygen targeting 94-98% SpO2; assist ventilations with BVM if inadequate
Midazolam 10 mg IM (65 kg x 0.2 mg/kg = 13 mg, capped at 10 mg max; no IV access)
Check blood glucose while still actively seizing

scenarioEvents.name: Seizure resolves after midazolam
scenarioEvents.description: Convulsive activity has stopped; patient is postictal with confusion, depressed but spontaneous respirations, and gradually returning responsiveness.
relatedChecklist: Reassess airway patency, breathing effectiveness, and neurologic status for transport

scenarioEvents.name: Seizure continues past 5 minutes
scenarioEvents.description: Convulsive activity persists five minutes after the first IM midazolam dose. Ventilation is becoming inadequate and the crew must weigh the risk of a repeat benzodiazepine dose against progressive hypoxia.
relatedChecklist: Weigh risk/benefit of a second benzodiazepine dose; consider medical direction consult
Prepare for advanced airway management if ventilation remains inadequate despite BVM support
